facts.statement: The genus Riparovenator contains only one known species, Riparovenator milnerae.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Riparovenator milnerae.

facts.statement: Spinosaurid fossils were uncovered between 2013 and 2017 at a beach near Chilton Chine in Britain.
facts.quote: Between 2013 and 2017, spinosaurid fossils were uncovered at the beach near the Chilton Chine before being brought to Dinosaur Isle.

facts.statement: Fossils now identified as Riparovenator were historically misidentified as belonging to the genus Baryonyx.
facts.quote: Such remains had historically been referred to Baryonyx but were understood later to represent two new species.

facts.statement: The species Riparovenator milnerae was formally named and described in 2021 by a team including Chris T. Barker, David W. E. Hone, and Darren Naish.
facts.quote: In 2021, the type species Riparovenator milnerae was named and described by a team of palaeontologists including Chris T. Barker, David W. E. Hone, Darren Naish, and others.

facts.statement: The genus name Riparovenator means 'riverbank hunter' in Latin.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Latin rīpārius,

facts.statement: The specific name milnerae honors Angela Milner, who died in August 2021.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Angela Milner, deceased in August 2021.

facts.statement: The holotype of Riparovenator includes premaxillary bodies, a disarticulated braincase, and a partial lacrimal and prefrontal bone.
facts.quote: The holotype remains of this taxon consist of IWCMS 2014.95.6 (premaxillary bodies), IWCMS 2014.96.1, 2; 2020.448.1, 2 (a disarticulated braincase), and IWCMS 2014.96.3 (a partial lacrimal and prefrontal).

facts.statement: Referred remains include a posterior nasal fragment and a series of twenty-two tail vertebrae, totaling around fifty bones.
facts.quote: Referred remains include a posterior nasal fragment (IWCMS 2014.95.7) and a caudal axial series of twenty-two vertebrae (IWCMS 2020.447.1-39), representing around fifty individual bones in total.

facts.statement: All known fossil material of Riparovenator was recovered from the Wessex Formation at Chilton Chine.
facts.quote: All of the material was recovered from rocks in the Chilton Chine of the Wessex Formation.

facts.statement: Riparovenator milnerae is estimated to be 10.6 meters long, up to 2.65 meters tall at the hip, and weigh between 4.3 and 4.8 tonnes.

facts.statement: Riparovenator is considered the second largest carnivorous theropod dinosaur in Europe, after Megalosaurus bucklandii.

facts.statement: Riparovenator likely fed on aquatic prey like fish and turtles, as well as terrestrial prey including young crocodiles, baby dinosaurs, and mammals.
facts.quote: Like most spinosaurids, it would have fed on aquatic prey as well as other terrestrial prey in these areas, such as fish, small turtles, young crocodiles, baby dinosaurs, and mammals.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that high diversity among spinosaurids in the same area may have been caused by environmental conditions that benefited their ecological niche.
facts.quote: Barker and colleagues suggested that high diversity within Spinosauridae in a given area may have been the result of environmental circumstances benefiting their niche.

facts.statement: It is debated whether similar and closely related spinosaurids could coexist by overlapping in ecological requirements rather than partitioning resources.
facts.quote: Barker and colleagues noted that this does not preclude that similar and closely related taxa could coexist and overlap in ecological requirements.

facts.statement: Barker et al. (2021) classified Ceratosuchops as the sister taxon to Riparovenator within the subfamily Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analysis, Barker et al. (2021) recovered Ceratosuchops within the Baryonychinae, as the sister taxon to the coeval Riparovenator.

facts.statement: In 2022, Sereno and colleagues tentatively proposed combining Ceratosuchops and Riparovenator into a single taxonomic unit.
facts.quote: In 2022, Sereno and colleagues tentatively combined Ceratosuchops and Riparovenator into a single taxonomic unit for their phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: Riparovenator is recovered as a member of the clade Ceratosuchopsini, closely related to Ceratosuchops and Suchomimus, with Ceratosuchops as its sister taxon.
